questions.question: Who among the following became the first Mughal emperor after defeating Ibrahim Lodi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Babur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Babur was the founder of the Mughal Empire and the first Mughal emperor in India.

 
 
• He became the first Mughal emperor after defeating Ibrahim Lodi​.
 
 
 
• **Humayun** was the second Mughal Emperor in India.
 
• **Akbar **was the third Mughal Emperor.
 
• **Jahangir** was the fourth Mughal Emperor.
 
• **Shah Jahan** was the fifth Mughal Emperor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first battle of Panipat was fought in 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• ​In 1526, the Mughal forces of Babur, the Timurid ruler of Kabulistan, defeated the much larger ruling army of Ibrahim Lodi, Sultan of Delhi.​
 
• Panipat was a legendary location where after 1526, multiple battles were fought between the Mughal and varying other forces.
 
• He was invited by Daulat Khan, the governor of Punjab, to invade the region and unsettle Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• Lodi’s army relied heavily on cavalry and especially on elephants, which in earlier times, could shock the enemy and rout them.
 
• This battle made the foundation of the Mughal dynasty in India.

a8:T

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of deforestation?

options.text: Decrease in level of ground water
Increase in pollution level on earth
Increase in level of oxygen in the atmosphere
Disturbance in the overall balance of nature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in level of oxygen in the atmosphere.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An increase in the level of oxygen in the atmosphere** is not a consequence of deforestation.
 
• Deforestation is a very broad term, which consists of cutting of trees including repeated lopping, felling, and removal of forest litter, browsing, grazing, and trampling of seedlings.
 
• **Consequences of Deforestation:-**
 
• Loss of Habitat
 
 
• 70% of land animals and plant species live in forests. 
 
• **Disturbance in the overall balance of nature.**
 
• The trees of the rainforest that provide shelter for some species also provide the canopy that regulates the temperature.
 
• Deforestation results in a more drastic temperature variation from day to night, much like a desert, which could prove fatal for many inhabitants. 
 
 
 
• Soil Erosion
 
 
• Trees help the land retain water and topsoil, which provides the rich nutrients to sustain additional forest life.
 
• Without forests, the soil erodes and washes away, causing farmers to move on and perpetuate the cycle.
 
 
 
• Desertification
 
 
• It is a transformation of once fertile land into a desert.
 
• **Decrease in level of groundwater.**
 
• It refers to the persistent degradation of dryland ecosystems by climatic variations and human activities.
 
• If trees are removed, the area can become much warmer and drier, which may result in desertification.
 
 
 
• Climate Change
 
 
• Trees and other plants absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as they grow.
 
• **Increase in pollution level on earth.**
 
• This is converted into carbon and stored in the plant’s branches, leaves, trunks, roots, and soil.
 
• When forests are cleared or burnt, the stored carbon is released into the atmosphere, mainly as carbon dioxide.
 
• This leads to climate change.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Causes of Deforestation: The most common reason for deforestation is the cutting of wood for fuel, lumber, and paper. Another important cause relates to the clearing of forest land for agriculture, including conversion to cropland and pasture. The main causes of deforestation are:

 
 
• Agriculture
 
• Shifting cultivation
 
• Demand for firewood
 
• Wood for industry and commercial use
 
• Urbanization and developmental projects
 
• Overgrazing of forests

questions.question: As per the Census of India–2011, there are ______ statutory towns in the country
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4,041.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Statutory Town** is one with a municipality, corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee.

 
 
• As per the 2011 Census, there are **4,041 such towns as against 3,799 in 2001.**
 
 
 
• A census town is one which is not statutorily notified and administered as a town, but whose population has attained urban characteristics.
 
 
• As per the 2011 Census, there are **3,784 Census Towns against 1,362 in 2001.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• A Census Town is an area with urban characteristics like

 
 
• A minimum population of 5,000
 
• At least 75% of the male main working force engaged in non-agricultural activities
 
• Population density of at least 400 persons per km2
 
 
 
• As per the 2011 Census, there are 3,784 Census Towns against 1,362 in 2001.
 
• Conversion of Census towns into statutory ULBs entitles states to Central assistance as per the guidelines of the 14th Finance Commission.
 
• Under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT), 50% weightage is given to the number of statutory towns in any State/UT in the allocation of funds among States/UTs.
 
• The state with the highest number of census towns in West Bengal with 780 towns.
 
• **Mizoram **has no census towns.

questions.question: The Scheme of Mega Food Park aims at providing a mechanism of direct linkage from farm to processing and then to consumer markets through a network of collection centres and primary processing centres. In which of the following states did Narendra Singh Tomar virtually inaugurate Mega Food Park in November 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union Minister for Food Processing Industries, Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Rural Development and Panchayati Raj virtually inaugurated Sukhjit Mega Food Park (MFP) at Phagwara in **Kapurthala district of Punjab.**
 
• It is the second operation mega food park in the state after International Mega Food Park, Fazilka. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ministry of Food Processing Industries is implementing Mega Food Park Scheme in the country since 2008.
 
• The Scheme of Mega Food Park aims at providing a mechanism to link agricultural production to the market by bringing together farmers, processors and retailers so as to ensure maximizing value addition, minimizing wastage, increasing farmers income and creating employment opportunities, particularly in the rural sector.
 
• The scheme aims to facilitate the establishment of a strong food processing industry backed by an efficient supply chain, which includes Collection Centres (CCs), Primary Processing Centers (PPCs), Central Processing Center (CPC) and Cold Chain infrastructure.
 
• The Mega Food Park Scheme is based on the “Cluster” approach. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The Mega Food Park project is implemented by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) which is a Body Corporate registered under the Companies Act. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• State Government, State Government entities and Cooperatives are not required to form a separate SPV for implementation of Mega Food Park project.
 
• So far following 21 Mega Food Parks are operational in the country.​

questions.question: In October 2020, World Bank expected India's GDP to contract by how much percent in the fiscal year 2020-21?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **9.6**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• GDP - **Gross Domestic Product **refers to sum total value of all final goods and services, produced in an accounting year, and measured at constant prices of a base year.
 
• There are **3** different methods to calculate GDP- 
 
 
• **Value Added Method**
 
• **Income Method**
 
• **Expenditure Method**
 
 
 
• GDP is an indicator of the economic outlook and growth prospects of a country. 
 
• In India, GDP is measured by **Central Statistical Office, **under the **Ministry of Statistics and Program Implementation.**
 
• GVA - Gross Value Added refers to the value of the number of goods and services produced in an economy minus value of inputs consumed in process of production. 
 
• GVA = Value of Output - Intermediate Consumption

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

questions.question: Water which is purified and fit for drinking is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**potable water.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Water which is purified and fit for drinking is known as **Potable water.**
 
• Potable water is water that has been either treated, cleaned or filtered and meets established drinking water standards or is assumed to be reasonably free of harmful bacteria and contaminants, and considered safe to drink or use in cooking and baking.
 
• **Examples of potable water** would be that from treated municipal water systems, water that has been UV filtered, water distilled, or purified by reverse osmosis.
 
• The total count of bacteria in potable water should not exceed **10 per cc.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Soft water is surface water that contains low concentrations of ions and in particular, is low in ions of calcium and magnesium.
 
• Hard water is surface water that contains more than 50 mg/l of calcium carbonate.
 
• Hard water has high mineral content.
 
• This is formed as water percolates into layers of calcium, chalk, or gypsum that are mainly composed of carbonates of calcium and magnesium, bicarbonates, and sulfates.

questions.question: The ________ Schedule of the Constitution of India added by the Constitution (Fifty-Second Amendment) Act, 1985 deals with the disqualification of a person for being a member of either house of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council of a State, on the ground of defection.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tenth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tenth Schedule** of the Constitution of India added by the Constitution (Fifty-Second Amendment) Act, 1985 deals with the disqualification of a person for being a member of either house of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council of a State, on the ground of defection.
 
• The Tenth Schedule popularly known as the Anti-Defection Act was included in the Constitution via the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 and sets the provisions for disqualification of elected members on the grounds of defection to another political party.
 
• The anti-defection law was enacted during the Rajiv Gandhi government in 1985. Parliament added it to the constitution in the year 1985. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• It was added in the Tenth Schedule. 
 
• According to 91st CAA, 2003, at least two-thirds of the members of a party have to be in favour of a "merger" for it to have validity in the eyes of the law. ** **
 
• The speaker or the chairman of the respective legislative house decide on disqualification arising out of defection.
